newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end stronger, renew August rally.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end stronger, renew August rally.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE

* Toronto stocks closed firmer, renewing the August rally after ending softer the past two days. * Boosted by consumer products, golds. * 83.6 million shares traded worth C$986.7 million.
Toronto stocks ended firmer on Wednesday, resuming their August winning run after a two-day breather.

"Canadian stocks, by and large, have been performing better than the U.S.," said John Kellett, Royal Bank of Canada's vice-president of equities. The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Index gained 10.2 points to close at 5184.1 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 1.1 points to end at 5712.4.
"We are nearing all-time highs on both sides of the border," said Richardson Greenshields of Canada analyst Josef Schachter in a market report.
The key TSE 300 Index has an all-time high of 5248 points while New York's record is 5833 points.

Toronto has added nearly 300 points since July 30, pausing only a few times in August including for the previous two days. "We've had a nice little recovery from a fairly aggressive correction" earlier this summer, Kellett said.

Trading has been brisk this week despite being historically one of the slowest periods of the year, ahead of the long holiday weekend. Canadian markets are closed on Monday, Sept. 2 for Labor Day. Volume was 83.6 million shares, worth C$986.7 million.
Rising stocks totalled 482, outpacing 426 falling issues. And 293 issues traded flat.
Nine of Toronto's 14 sub-indices climbed, led by consumer products, golds and media issues. Weakening sectors included base metals, real estate and oils.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* Canadian 88 Energy Corp topped the most actives, rising 0.33 to 5.30 on 3.4 million shares after news of "significant" reserves in an Alberta oil well.
* Corel Corp jumped 0.85 to 13.40 in heavy turnover, boosted by a deal to bundle its software with new home computers shipped by Compaq Computer Corp.
-- Lydia Zajc, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100
